title: Back epic_27_story_27_8's tutor/rules security-boundary tests with real rule evaluation, not substring matching

evidence.quote:
// as Group A — the `fake_firebase_security_rules` package cannot evaluate
  // `request.auth.uid` comparisons dynamically, but string-scanning the rules

why: The file's own comment admits the dynamic rules-emulation package can't evaluate request.auth.uid, so the 'LOAD-BEARING security invariant' tests (line 199) fall back to scanning firestore.rules TEXT for substrings. A rule edit that inserts a bypass while preserving the substrings — e.g. `allow create: if isOwner(uid) || request.auth != null;` — still contains 'isOwner(uid)', still omits 'isTutorOf', and would pass every assertion here while granting any authenticated user write access to completions. Per the audit baseline, the real emulator-based rules suite (firestore_rules.test.mjs) is currently soft-skipped in `make ci` (TQ-9, already known) — so this Dart text-matching suite may be the only thing CI runs today for the tutor-write-block boundary this file calls load-bearing.
recommendation: Assert the tutor-write-block and owner-write invariants against the actual Firestore Rules emulator (@firebase/rules-unit-testing) with real auth contexts (assertFails/assertSucceeds), not string containment on the rules source; keep the text-scan tests only as a fast pre-check, not the sole gate.
acceptance_criteria: An emulator-backed test asserts a tutor-authenticated write to completions/{completionId} is denied and an owner-authenticated write succeeds.
CI runs this test unconditionally (ties into the existing TQ-9 soft-skip fix).
